about.title: Covina Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Covina's mix of warehouses, retail centers, and small manufacturing shops along corridors like Citrus Avenue and San Bernardino Road means workplace injuries here run the gamut from forklift accidents to falls on uneven loading docks. Most of the time, California law channels these injuries through workers' compensation, which pays medical bills and partial wages regardless of who caused the accident, but doesn't cover pain and suffering. What often gets missed is that a third party — a subcontractor, a delivery driver, a defective equipment manufacturer, or even another motorist if you're injured driving for work near a busy stretch like Grand Avenue — might carry separate legal responsibility. That separate claim runs on a different clock and different rules than workers' comp. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect injured workers in Covina with an independent attorney who can look at both angles and explain, in plain terms, what applies to your situation and what doesn't.

whyChoose.title: Why Covina Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Always Obvious
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, many injured workers assume that's the end of the story. An independent attorney can look for a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — who may owe you a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early On
items.desc: California requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting matched with an attorney quickly helps make sure that step, and everything after it, gets handled properly.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and You Have Options
items.desc: It's against California law for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on your rights if you're worried about how reporting an injury might be received.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site off San Bernardino Road — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your exclusive path against your employer regardless of fault, so that's typically the first claim to file. But if a third party — like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment supplier — contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate injury claim. An independent attorney can review the specifics and tell you which paths apply.

items.question: What if I was injured driving for work near Grand Avenue or Badillo Street?
items.answer: If another driver caused the crash while you were performing job duties, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a separate claim against that driver. Since Covina's crash data shows collisions cluster on weekday afternoons, particularly Thursdays, this scenario isn't uncommon for local delivery or service workers. An attorney can help sort out how the two claims interact.
